firstScreen.notes: 1440-first.jpg: signature visible at once (Plate I drawn inside the mill-window arch), one loud primary (signal-yellow Call) plus a quiet outline 'Price my wall', phone in header and hero, Sample-labelled proof line. But the h1 'Old plaster, kept where it can be.' carries no place; Manchester only lives in the small italic eyebrow (-0.5). The band below the hero peeks as 57px of empty cream, no content (-0.5 partial, held at 8.5 by the signature). 390-first.jpg: h1 4 lines, both actions above the fold, but the plate is pushed below the fold so the phone first screen shows only the arch rim.

distinctiveness.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: Era Plates in hero, 1890/1950/2005 story, micro-plates on all nine service cards, Plate V ice-dam drawing in the season band, the identifier key, the patch sketch in prices, and the empty Plate IV in the footer; arched review cards echo the mill window. Nothing like drywall-A (photo + tape frame, green) or drywall-B (dark, mono, level tags). Deductions: middle-dot meta strings in the hero proof line and every plate caption (1440-first.jpg) -0.5; brick + cream sits close to the 'cream + terracotta default' tell, saved by the slate/navy bands.

type.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: Newsreader + Libre Franklin is a fitting pair, the italic serif break quote is a real scale-contrast moment,   used against heading orphans, curly quotes. Deductions: section ledes ('Before anyone says "gut it"…', 'Small visits get the same care…') are set small and grey and float at the right baseline of the h2 (1440-rm-full.jpg) -0.5; more than 5 sizes in one view in the price sheet (label caps, select, slider ticks, price h, note, visits table, typical ranges, steps: 1440-scroll-75.jpg) -0.5; the giant pale era numerals 1890/1950/2005 are almost background-tone, which reads washed out rather than intentional.

layout.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: real rhythm (brick hero → cream story → paper services grid → slate season → navy break → cream identifier → paper prices sheet → brick reviews → cream area → navy contact → brick footer), dense services and quiet break both present. Deductions: the era story leaves big dead space, empty right column under each era block and the whole left half beside the Ray O. quote (1440-scroll-25.jpg) -0.5; slate season band runs straight into the navy break and reads as one dark block (1440-scroll-50.jpg; the wave rule helps but the tones are too close) -0.5; centred prices h2 is the one centred heading on a left-aligned page (1440-rm-full.jpg).

photo.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg and 390-rm-full.jpg: there is not one photograph on the page. The concept promises 'mill-window arch photo frames' and a hover where 'the photo pans 2% up'; the arches hold drawings only. The drawings are excellent, but a homeowner never sees a real wall, crack, lath or finished room, and the footer has to admit 'Drawings stand in for project photos'. Scored against the 8 anchor for a missing medium, not for bad frames.

copy.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: real trade nouns (keys, wood lath, rock lath, plaster washers, brown coat, paper tape), honest 'it depends' answers ('Reset it in March and it stays reset'), the hero sub names the three walls, every review/price/rating/promise/licence tagged Sample, facts match facts.json. Deductions: the primary action has several names ('Price my wall', 'Price it' on cards, 'Ask us to look at it' in the identifier: 1440-rm-full.jpg) -0.5; era dates disagree: story plates say c.1950 rock lath and c.2005 board, the identifier key says rock lath 'about 1920 to 1969' and board '1970 on' (1440-rm-full.jpg) -0.5, offset by the voice.

mobile.notes: 390-first.jpg: h1 4 lines, both buttons above the fold, sticky Call/Text/Price my wall bar. 390-full.jpg: no sideways scroll (render.json scrollWidth 390, 320 also clean). Deductions: price ranges break mid-range ('$900 to / $2,300') in the typical-ranges list (390-rm-full.jpg) -0.5; the hero is the desktop stack, plate pushed below the fold rather than re-cut for the phone (390-first.jpg).

a11y.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg and 390-rm-full.jpg: every word and every plate visible with reduced motion; inputs visibly labelled (THE JOB, HOW BIG IS THE DAMAGE?, YOUR ZIP CODE); forced-colors block present in dist/index.html; render.json no errors. Watch the pale era numerals (1440-rm-full.jpg): if they are not aria-hidden they fail contrast.

motion.notes: 1440-first.jpg catches the arch fanlight muntins mid-draw and Plate I built; 1440-full.jpg shows the era plates as bare stud slabs before their layers build, and 1440-scroll-25.jpg shows Plate III complete, so the plates draw layer by layer on scroll. The motion explains the wall's construction, which is the thesis. Season bands, identifier, slider-driven patch sketch add interaction. Not 9.5: no evidence of a distinct hover language in the frames.

wow.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg: the wall-era identifier picks a plate in the signature's language and the footer's empty Plate IV says it is drawn from your answer; the patch sizer turns a slider into a drawn hole and a visits table with a printable price (1440-scroll-75.jpg). Two connected moments, tied to the trade.

polish.notes: dist/index.html: apple-touch, og:image, JSON-LD, print stylesheet for the price sheet, forced-colors. 1440-rm-full.jpg: one rule weight, square corners throughout, arched review cards and Plate IV footer give a designed close.

elevate.move: Deliver the promised pairing: put real approved library frames inside the mill-window arches beside each era plate (horsehair keys behind a broken plaster edge, rock lath, taped board), so every drawing has its photograph and the drawing-to-photo pair becomes the story's rhythm; make the hero arch hold the photo with Plate I drawn over its lower half.

Put Manchester into the h1's world: set the hero as a surveyor's plate title ('Manchester walls, 1890 to now' as the plate heading above the h1 or a city line in the h1) and on 390 re-cut the hero so a cropped Plate I sits beside the h1 instead of below the fold.
